solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grab-bag mostly packed with nutrition first

indicators.note: packed with means the word for bag has something stuffed inside it
mostly means the word for bag loses its final couple of letters

parts.note: a satchel is a shoulder bag carried by schoolchildren

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word nutrition is taken

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a bag of health food, prioritising nutrition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims EL from SATCHEL to leave SATCH, and the N from 'nutrition first' goes in after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab and to snatch are synonyms: both mean to seize something quickly.

clue.text: Passover — when pulpit lament centres on my oath

indicators.note: centres means the middle letters of each of the four preceding words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A preacher's Passover sermon is focused on a solemn vow.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word gives its central letters: SO from Passover, HE from when, LP from pulpit, ME from lament. 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of solemn swearing: 'my oath' is an Australian idiom with the same force as calling on God to witness.

clue.text: Being slightly car-mad, I'll opt for small armoured one

indicators.note: being slightly something means being only part of it, so the answer is a run of letters lying within these words

explanation.surface: A driver who is a little obsessed with cars picks a small armoured vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run straight through 'car-mad, I'll opt', ignoring the hyphen and punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American mammal is protected by bony plates, and it is quite small, so the description of it as a little armoured creature fits.

clue.text: Short cut for hands

indicators.note: short means the name of the haircut is cut short, losing its second half

parts.note: a crew cut is a close-cropped style of haircut

explanation.surface: A quick route to finding workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short cut' looks like a quicker route. The crew cut is itself a short haircut, so the blog reads a double definition; either way the name loses its second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company of sailors is its crew, and hands are workers, especially those aboard a ship.

clue.text: Most outsanding rates get adjusted

indicators.note: adjusted means the letters are altered and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Interest rates that change to be the best on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'outsanding' is a typo for 'outstanding'.
explanation.definitionFit: The greatest thing is the best of all, so it is the most outstanding: a superlative synonym.

clue.text: Turned in tradition, turned in revolutionary

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the word for revolutionary

parts.note: red is the usual crossword word for a revolutionary or communist

indicators.note: turned means the word for tradition is read backwards

parts.note: a rite is a traditional ceremony

explanation.surface: Something keeps getting turned round, in a custom and in a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned in' at the start looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition; the second 'turned' signals the reversal and the second 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To have turned in is to have gone to bed for the night, the same as having retired.

clue.text: Environmentally operated a time-piece from Russian city bar

indicators.note: a piece from means only part of the city's name is used, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: Moscow is the Russian capital
to bar a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: A green-powered timepiece from a bar in Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is short; the whole clue describes the device. MOSC is MOSCOW minus OW.
explanation.definitionFit: This brand of timepiece is powered by small changes in temperature and air pressure, so it runs on its surroundings.

clue.text: River full of a lot of mud and discharge

indicators.note: full of means the river's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a favourite crossword river

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word mud is used, losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A muddy river discharging its flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, England; 'a lot of mud' loses the M.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude is to ooze out or give off, which is a synonym of discharge as a verb.

clue.text: Fancy this mid-thirties garment?

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or made up, so these letters are worked into a new order
mid means the central letters of the word thirties are taken

explanation.surface: Someone in their thirties wonders whether to wear this item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: THIS plus RT, the two central letters of 'thirties', rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sleeved collarless top shaped like a letter is a basic item of clothing.

clue.text: Slip up in supplement to bill on opening night

indicators.note: in means the word up is placed inside the other word

parts.note: lovers 'bill and coo', so coo is the word that goes with bill

indicators.note: opening means only the first letter of the word night is taken

explanation.surface: A mistake in the theatre programme insert on a show's first night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' is not a theatre poster: the idiom 'bill and coo' (to kiss and murmur lovingly) supplies COO. 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a small slip of paper, a voucher or form torn off and handed in.

clue.text: Successfully negotiate what one gets for fixing nails

definitions.meaning: to reach an agreement after long discussion

definitions.text: what one gets for fixing nails
definitions.meaning: read literally, you take out a hammer when there are nails to drive in

explanation.definitionFit: To hammer out a deal is an idiom for settling it after hard bargaining; literally one brings out a hammer to drive nails.

clue.text: See 19
Reverse into crocodile pool

indicators.note: reverse means the letters found are read backwards
into means the letters needed lie inside the word crocodile

explanation.surface: Someone backs away into a pool with a crocodile in it.
explanation.walkthrough: ODIL lies inside 'crocodile'; read backwards it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, a common British word.

clue.text: Played worst in sort of mint Lycra, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the mint word

parts.note: spearmint is a kind of mint, so the first part of its name stands for it

indicators.note: played means the letters of worst are moved about, as if played with

explanation.surface: An athlete performed badly while wearing mint-green Lycra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' looks like the sport, but it signals the anagram of 'worst'; 'sort of mint' is spearmint, cut to its first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a stretchy fabric used for athletic clothing, so it is an example of gear for exercise, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Black singer captures wanderers' hearts in fairy tale

indicators.note: captures means the singer's name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Cilla Black was a Liverpool singer and TV presenter

indicators.note: hearts means the central letters of the word wanderers are taken

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned singer enchants travellers in a fairy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black singer' is Cilla Black, a 1960s Liverpool pop singer and TV host, not a description of race; 'hearts' takes the five central letters of 'wanderers'.
explanation.definitionFit: This rags-to-riches story of a girl, a glass slipper and a prince is one of the best-known fairy tales.

clue.text: A lot of factory is only half working

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill

indicators.note: only half means just the first half of the word is is used

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: Much of a factory is running at half capacity.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of 'is' gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: A million is a very large number, so it is used loosely to mean a great many.

clue.text: Back staff keeping 100% of the money

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled piece is read in reverse
keeping means the staff word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
one hundred per cent is all of something

explanation.surface: Supporting employees by letting them keep all the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support and 'staff' like employees; 'Back' reverses the whole container, and 'of the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is a unit of currency, so it is an example of money.

clue.text: In a river, heartless Nelson has what he needs to weigh anchor

indicators.note: in means the following letters go inside the a-and-river pair
heartless means the middle of the name Nelson is removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: an ounce is a unit of weight, something needed to weigh things

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson, on a river, needs to raise anchor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weigh anchor' looks like the sailing phrase, but 'anchor' alone is the definition, a news presenter; 'he' is Nelson, who needs a unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A news anchor presents a broadcast, and a broadcast presenter is called an announcer.

clue.text: Lid with stye's treated artificially

indicators.note: treated means the letters are processed and reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An eyelid with a stye has been medically treated.
explanation.walkthrough: LID and STYES rearranged; 'with' is a link word. The definition is loose: an adverb standing for 'done artificially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylised art follows conventions rather than nature, so it is rendered in an artificial, non-realistic manner.

clue.text: Speaking of how to drum excitedly

indicators.note: excitedly means the letters jump about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A lesson in how to beat a drum with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: News that spreads by word of mouth travels through people talking to each other, so the phrase stands for speaking.

clue.text: Tomcat maybe one having scraps

definitions.meaning: the F-14 Tomcat was a US Navy combat jet, an example of a military aircraft
a scrap is a fight, so someone who scraps is a brawler

explanation.surface: A male cat that gets into fights.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is both a combat aircraft such as the Tomcat jet and a person who gets into fights.

clue.text: Fair target for shy person

parts.note: at a British fair a shy is a stall where you throw balls at nuts set on posts, so the nut is the fair target; the surface suggests a timid person being picked on

explanation.surface: A timid person is a legitimate target.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a fairground game in which balls are thrown to knock coconuts off stands; 'shy' means throw, not timid.
explanation.definitionFit: At a fairground throwing stall the prize nuts are the targets, so the answer is literally the fair's target for a shy.

clue.text: Subject of legendary royal waves

parts.note: the legend tells of an English king who sat on the shore and commanded the tide to halt; the surface suggests a monarch waving to crowds

explanation.surface: A monarch famous for waving to crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' are sea waves, not royal hand gestures.
explanation.definitionFit: This eleventh-century Danish king of England is the subject of the story of ordering the incoming sea to stop.

clue.text: Burning the 4 Gospels helps terrorist leaders

parts.note: the clue points at the answer to 4-across; the boxer Muhammad Ali called himself by that title

indicators.note: leaders means the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Setting fire to the four Gospels helps terrorist chiefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 4' points to 4-across: 'The Greatest' was Muhammad Ali's nickname, giving ALI. The 4 Gospels are not the four books of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alight is on fire, so the word is a synonym of burning.

clue.text: Middle England furious about first lady exerting influence

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go round the first lady
middle means the central letter of the word England is taken

parts.note: raging means furious
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Middle England is angry about the President's wife exerting influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle England', the political phrase for conservative suburban Britain, gives just its central letter; 'first lady' is the Bible's first woman, not a president's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Leveraging means using one's power or position to gain an advantage, which is a way of exerting influence.

clue.text: Second in command boards wrong express

indicators.note: boards means the letter gets on, inside the word for wrong, as a passenger boards a ship

parts.note: vice is wrongdoing or immorality

indicators.note: second in means the second letter of the word command is taken

explanation.surface: A deputy commander boards an express train going the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second in command' looks like a deputy, but it gives O, which goes inside VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to express it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Lies about flight's destination, maybe

definitions.meaning: nonsense or untruths, as in talking rubbish
a dart has flights on its tail, and darts aim for the centre of the board

explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for nonsense or lies, and the bull is the bullseye at the centre of a dartboard, where a dart in flight aims.

clue.text: Degree next to minute

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
by means beside, as in standing by the door

explanation.surface: An academic degree sits next to a tiny measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' means tiny, not sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby used as an adjective means very small, as in baby carrots, so it fits minute in the sense of tiny.

clue.text: Roast? Yes and no

parts.note: to cook under direct heat is close to roasting but not quite the same, and to roast someone by harsh questioning is also close; so it is roasting and not roasting

explanation.walkthrough: The hint is two near-misses: cooking under a heated element is not quite roasting, and interrogating someone hard is a kind of figurative roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill is to cook by direct radiant heat, which is like roasting without being it, and also to question someone relentlessly.

clue.text: Four kings start to abuse charters

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of the word to is taken
abuse means the letters of charters are mistreated and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Four monarchs begin to tear up their royal charters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' is the first letter of 'to', T, not a phrase meaning 'begin to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrarchy was rule by four people, as in the late Roman Empire, so its rulers were four kings in effect.

clue.text: References unfinished dissertation about a Biblical city

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round the other pieces
unfinished means the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a thesis is a long academic dissertation
Ur of the Chaldees was Abraham's birthplace in the Bible

explanation.surface: An incomplete doctoral thesis citing an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur of the Chaldees is the Biblical city; 'unfinished' drops the last letter of the dissertation word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms; the Latin plural form names several such reference works.

clue.text: Cross at being taken in by trophy bride

indicators.note: being taken in by means the answer is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is angry at being fooled by a glamorous young wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it means a mix; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross between two breeds or species is a hybrid, so the noun senses are synonyms.
